stories.title: Jamia due to resume offline classes on Tuesday 10 November; exams from Monday 16 November reported
stories.body: Jamia Millia Islamia is due to resume offline classes for undergraduate and postgraduate programmes on Tuesday 10 November, after a campus protest over the students' union, according to reports published on Friday 30 October. Careers360 reports that exams are to be held offline from Monday 16 to Saturday 21 November, and that the administration has set 15 May 2027 as the deadline to finalise the students' union constitution. The reports also say pending action against protesters is to be withdrawn and attendance made compulsory. No notice from Jamia confirming that classes restarted on 10 November was found.
stories.check: The reports conflict. Careers360 (30 Oct) says second-semester exams run 16-21 Nov; ThePrint's headline refers to second mid-term exams from 16 Nov. A second Careers360 piece cites a 29 Oct registrar's notice with 2 Nov as the restart date. No official Jamia notice could be opened. Confirm the restart and exam dates with Jamia.

stories.title: Two Jamia girls' hostels mark BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week with pledges, plantation and Eco-Diwali
stories.body: Two Jamia Millia Islamia girls' hostels have reported activities for BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week 2026, under Mission LiFE, in press releases dated Monday 9 November. At the Begum Hazrat Mahal Girls' Hostel, students took a sustainability pledge, ran a plantation drive using plastic bottles as planters, and held a debate on topics including single-use plastic and e-waste. At the Hall of Girls' Residence (Old), activities included a panel discussion and a Green Rally, and an Eco-Diwali gathering on Sunday 8 November drew over 150 residents, who pledged to avoid firecrackers and used earthen diyas and LED lights.
stories.check: Both accounts are the university's own releases (6186 and 6188). The release pages themselves did not open in this run; details are from the PDFs. The Begum Hazrat Mahal event is dated only as 'today' in its release.

stories.title: Jamia and NCPUL publish book on the writings of Urdu scholar Kalimuddin Ahmad
stories.body: Jamia Millia Islamia's Department of Urdu and the National Council for Promotion of Urdu Language (NCPUL) have published a book from a national seminar on the writings of Kalimuddin Ahmad, according to a Jamia press release dated Monday 9 November. The seminar was held on Monday 27 April 2026. The release says the book is edited by Prof. Kausar Mazhari, head of the department, and contains 22 scholarly articles, a keynote by Prof. Shafey Kidwai of Aligarh and an editor's preface. It describes the volume as a reference for teachers and scholars.
stories.check: Single source: the university's own release (6189). Publication or availability details are not given in the release.

stories.title: Jamia report on 'Rethinking Southern Urbanism' programme held on 8 October
stories.body: Jamia Millia Islamia has issued a report, dated Monday 9 November, on a one-day programme titled 'Rethinking Southern Urbanism', organised by the Calcutta Research Group with the MMAJ Academy of International Studies at Jamia. The release says the programme took place on Thursday 8 October and asked what a distinct Southern urbanism could mean. It lists a public lecture by Prof. Awadhendra Sharan of CSDS on how breath, pollution, disease and climate have shaped city planning, followed by two book discussions in the afternoon.
stories.check: Single source: the university's own release (6185). The event is a month old; the news is the release. The release page showed only a title and PDF link.

stories.title: Jamia Middle School holds annual science, mathematics and social science exhibition
stories.body: Jamia Middle School held its Annual Exhibition 2026 on Thursday 22 October, according to a Jamia press release dated Monday 9 November. Student projects were shown in science, mathematics, social science, and art and craft, with first, second and third prizes in each of four categories and extra consolation prizes in science because of the number of entries. Judges came from Syed Abid Husain Senior Secondary School. Prof. Mary Tahir, Dean of the Faculty of Sciences, was among the guests, and the headmistress thanked the Vice-Chancellor and Registrar.
stories.check: Single source: the university's own release (6187). The event is more than two weeks old; the news is the release.
